review:
UFC 332 was a finish-heavy card: 11 of 14 bouts ended inside the distance, and 11 were KO/TKOs, with only two decisions (Silva over Wang, Soldic over Williams). The model called 11 of 14 winners (log loss 0.47), the closing line 11 of 11 priced bouts (0.365) and the blend 9 of 11 (0.338). On the season (37 cards, 433 bouts) the model sits at 0.623 log loss against the market's 0.568 and the blend's 0.572, so the line is still the benchmark to beat.

The model's method numbers were the story. It expected about 5 KO/TKOs among the 13 graded bouts and got 11 (z +3.5), and expected about 6 decisions and got 2 (z -2.5). Claude's picks leaned further toward finishes than the model's and won the method argument 3 of 4 times, finishing 20 points to the model's 17 (11 winners to 10). The one winner override was a hit. One card is not enough to re-weight anything (13 of the 100 bouts needed), but if the finish skew holds over more cards the automatic method adjustment will pick it up.

The bouts that mattered: Ribovics over Green (model 81%, line 64%) was a first-round KO, a rare case where the model was right and the line was wrong. McGhee over Romero was the line's win (model 55%, market 80%) and Nolan over McGee (model 85%) a confident hit. Naurdiev beat Vettori on the cards, a pick the market had at 53%, and the model at 37% missed it. Hernandez over Dos Anjos was another confident model hit.

Your notes: you said the card had many early finishes and would look anomalous, and the numbers agree, since the decision rate was far below the norm, so treat the KO skew as partly noise. Your note on Vettori (chin will fail soon, but Naurdiev gassed and was still hittable) fits the scouting read on Naurdiev's cardio. Your read that Dos Anjos is pretty much done and that Soldic looked hittable are useful for future reads: Soldic won by decision, but he did not dominate. Your notes on Pinas's power, Smith's ground and pound, and Imanol's aggression are folded into their reports as owner's notes.
